options.text: A condition where the heart has too many chambers
An infection of the heart valves
A condition where the coronary arteries become narrowed by fatty deposits, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle

questions.explanation: Coronary heart disease occurs when fatty deposits (atheroma) build up in the coronary arteries, narrowing them and reducing blood flow to the heart muscle, which can lead to a heart attack.

options.text: The build-up of fatty deposits (plaques) inside artery walls
A type of heart rhythm disorder

questions.explanation: Atherosclerosis is the build-up of fatty plaques (atheroma) on the inner walls of arteries, making them narrower and less elastic, which restricts blood flow and can lead to clots.

questions.stem: What is a stent used for?

options.text: To keep a narrowed or blocked coronary artery open

questions.explanation: A stent is a small mesh tube inserted into a narrowed coronary artery to hold it open, restoring blood flow to the heart muscle and reducing the risk of a heart attack.

questions.stem: Which lifestyle factor increases the risk of cardiovascular disease?
questions.explanation: Smoking increases the risk of cardiovascular disease by damaging the lining of arteries, increasing blood pressure, and making blood more likely to clot.
Statins are drugs that reduce the amount of cholesterol produced by the liver, lowering blood cholesterol levels and reducing the risk of fatty deposits forming in arteries.

questions.stem: What happens during a heart attack?

options.text: A coronary artery becomes completely blocked, cutting off blood supply to part of the heart muscle

questions.explanation: A heart attack occurs when a coronary artery becomes blocked (often by a blood clot forming on a fatty plaque). The heart muscle supplied by that artery is starved of oxygen and may be damaged or die.

questions.stem: How can a person reduce their risk of cardiovascular disease?

options.text: By exercising regularly, eating a healthy diet, not smoking, and maintaining a healthy weight

questions.explanation: Risk can be reduced through regular exercise, a diet low in saturated fat and salt, not smoking, maintaining a healthy weight, and moderating alcohol intake.
